alerts.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 12:56PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
At 1256 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Grand Junction, moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Grand Junction, Palisade, Cameo, Fruitvale, Clifton, Orchard Mesa,
and Redlands.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 70 in Colorado between mile markers 27 and 41, and
between mile markers 45 and 60.
U.S. Highway 50 in Colorado between mile markers 32 and 34.
Colorado 65 between mile markers 53 and 61.
Colorado 141 near mile marker 162.

alerts.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 2 at 12:37PM MDT until September 2 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Mesa County in west central Colorado...

* Until 330 PM MDT.

* At 1237 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 3 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.2 to 0.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of creeks, arroyos, and streams, streets
and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Grand Junction, Fruita and Colorado National Monument.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Devils Canyon, Monument Canyon, and Wedding Canyon

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 11:28AM MDT until September 2 at 2:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Mesa County in west central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 230 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks, streams, arroyos and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1126 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 0.3 and 0.8 inches of rain have
fallen. Rainfall rates of 1 to 3 inches per hour are expected
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Layton Wash, Dry Gulch, Reed Wash, Lipan Wash, Adobe Creek,
Coyote Wash, Big Salt Wash and Little Salt Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Fruita and Loma.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Aloft, the jet stream will move across the area and with deeper mixing expected, some gusty winds of 30 to 40 mph will be possible this afternoon and through the end of the week. Humidities will remain above any critical fire weather thresholds so do not anticipate any critical fire weather
